plan.title: JWT Authentication System — Login, Register, Refresh, Sessions, Middleware

task.description:
Create server/app/auth/jwt.py — JWT token creation and verification.
Implementation: - Use python-jose (jose library) with HS256 algorithm. - SECRET_KEY loaded from config module (not os.environ directly). - create_access_token(user_id: UUID, role: str) -> str: 24h expiry (from settings auth.jwt_expiry_minutes=1440). - create_refresh_token(user_id: UUID) -> str: 30d expiry (from settings auth.jwt_refresh_expiry_days=30). - verify_token(token: str) -> dict: decode and validate, raise on expired/invalid. - Token payload: sub (user_id as string), role, exp, iat, jti (unique ID for refresh token tracking).
Create server/app/auth/password.py — Password hashing with passlib bcrypt. - hash_password(password: str) -> str: bcrypt hash, cost factor 12. - verify_password(plain: str, hashed: str) -> bool: bcrypt verify. - generate_temp_password() -> str: secure random 16-char password using secrets module.
task.verification: create_access_token returns a valid JWT decodable by verify_token. Token expires after configured duration. hash_password output is verifiable by verify_password. generate_temp_password returns a 16-char string. No os.environ access for SECRET_KEY (loaded via config).
task.done-condition: JWT tokens are created with HS256 and verified correctly. Tokens include sub, role, exp, iat, jti claims. Passwords are bcrypt-hashed with cost factor 12. Temp passwords are 16 chars from secrets module.

task.description:
Create server/app/auth/middleware.py — FastAPI authentication dependencies.
Implementation: - get_current_user(token: str = Depends(oauth2_scheme), db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db)) -> User: Extracts user from JWT Bearer token. Returns User ORM object. Raises 401 on invalid/expired token. Uses OAuth2PasswordBearer(tokenUrl="/api/v1/auth/login"). - require_admin(current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user)) -> User: Calls get_current_user internally. Raises 403 if user.role != "admin". Returns User. - Check if session is revoked: look up the jti in sessions table, reject if is_revoked=True.
Export both dependencies from server/app/auth/__init__.py.
task.verification: get_current_user raises HTTPException(401) on missing/invalid token. require_admin raises HTTPException(403) when user.role != "admin". OAuth2PasswordBearer tokenUrl points to /api/v1/auth/login. Session revocation check is present (lookup jti in sessions table).
task.done-condition: get_current_user decodes JWT, fetches user from DB, checks session not revoked, returns User ORM object. require_admin additionally checks role=="admin" and raises 403 if not. Both are FastAPI Depends-compatible.

task.description:
Create server/app/services/auth.py — Auth business logic (login, register, refresh, change-password, sessions).
Service functions: - login(db, username, password) -> TokenResponse: Verify credentials. Create session record. Return access + refresh tokens + user. - register(db, username, email, password) -> TokenResponse: First user becomes admin (role="admin"). If users exist and allow_registration=false, raise 403. Hash password. Create user + session. Return tokens. - refresh_token(db, refresh_token_str) -> TokenResponse: Verify refresh token. Check session not revoked. Rotate: revoke old session, create new. Return new access + refresh token pair. - change_password(db, user_id, current_password, new_password) -> None: Verify current password. Hash new password. Update user. Clear must_change_password flag. - get_user_profile(db, user_id) -> User: Return user by ID. - update_user_profile(db, user_id, updates) -> User: Update email, display_name, title (username immutable). - list_user_sessions(db, user_id) -> list[Session]: Active sessions for user. - revoke_session(db, user_id, session_id) -> None: Cannot revoke own current session. Set is_revoked=True.
All functions receive AsyncSession as first arg. No direct DB calls outside this module.
task.verification: login returns TokenResponse with access_token, refresh_token, user. register: first user gets role="admin"; subsequent users with allow_registration=false get 403. refresh rotates tokens (old session revoked, new created). change_password clears must_change_password flag. revoke_session prevents revoking own session.
task.done-condition: All 8 auth service functions implemented with correct business rules. First-user-is-admin logic works. Refresh token rotation revokes old session. Password change clears must_change_password. Session revocation blocks self-revocation. Runnable check: `grep -c "^async def " server/app/services/auth.py` returns 8. Integration coverage: `pytest server/tests/integration/test_auth.py -v` exits 0 after PLAN-1-7 is complete.

dimension.name: scope
dimension.rationale: Single file but 8 functions with business logic

dimension.name: testing
dimension.rationale: Many edge cases: first user, registration disabled, token reuse

dimension.name: decomposability
dimension.rationale: Functions are interdependent (login creates sessions used by refresh)

task.description:
Create server/app/api/auth.py — Thin route handlers for all auth endpoints.
Routes (all under /api/v1/auth prefix): - POST /login (response_model=TokenResponse): body=LoginRequest, calls auth_service.login. - POST /register (response_model=TokenResponse): body=RegisterRequest, calls auth_service.register. - POST /refresh (response_model=TokenResponse): body={refresh_token: str}, calls auth_service.refresh_token. - POST /change-password (status_code=204): body=ChangePasswordRequest, requires get_current_user. Calls auth_service.change_password. - GET /me (response_model=UserResponse): requires get_current_user. Returns current user profile. - PATCH /me (response_model=UserResponse): body=UserUpdateRequest, requires get_current_user. Calls auth_service.update_user_profile. - PATCH /me/avatar (status_code=501): stub returning 501 Not Implemented (Phase 3+). - GET /sessions (response_model=list[SessionResponse]): requires get_current_user. Calls auth_service.list_user_sessions. - DELETE /sessions/{session_id} (status_code=204): requires get_current_user. Calls auth_service.revoke_session.
Every protected route: Depends(get_current_user). Every route: response_model declared on decorator. Thin handlers: validate input, call service, return response. No DB calls.
Register router in server/app/main.py with prefix="/api/v1/auth" and tags=["auth"].
task.verification: All 9 routes registered under /api/v1/auth prefix. Every protected route has Depends(get_current_user). Every route has response_model in decorator. No DB calls in route handlers (grep for session.execute/scalar in api/auth.py returns nothing). `curl POST /api/v1/auth/register` with first user returns 200 with tokens. `curl POST /api/v1/auth/login` with valid creds returns 200 with tokens.
task.done-condition: All 9 auth endpoints operational. POST /register creates admin for first user, returns 403 when registration disabled. POST /login returns access+refresh tokens. POST /refresh rotates tokens. GET /me returns user profile. All protected routes require valid JWT.

dimension.name: testing
dimension.rationale: Each endpoint needs happy + error path

plan.dependencies: PLAN-1-4 depends on PLAN-1-3 (needs User + Session models, Pydantic schemas, DB session)

decision.choice: Used datetime.UTC alias (Python 3.11+) instead of datetime.timezone.utc
decision.rationale: ruff UP017 flagged datetime.timezone.utc as fixable to datetime.UTC; project targets Python 3.12 so datetime.UTC is available and preferred.
decision.alternatives-considered: datetime.timezone.utc (rejected: ruff UP017 violation on target Python version)

decision.choice: Suppressed ruff B008 for Depends() calls with # noqa: B008
decision.rationale: FastAPI's dependency injection pattern requires Depends() in function default args. This is intentional and idiomatic FastAPI — not a bug. B008 is a false positive in this context.
decision.alternatives-considered: Module-level singletons (rejected: FastAPI DI works through default arg inspection); restructuring (rejected: would break FastAPI's DI resolution)

decision.choice: Removed private _create_session helper; inlined session creation in each function
decision.rationale: The helper was never called after implementation revealed that session creation varies slightly per call site (login has session_id pre-generated to create refresh token before session exists). Inlining removes unused code and the count satisfies the plan's done-condition of exactly 8 async def functions.
decision.alternatives-considered: Keep helper (rejected: unused, count would exceed 8 and violate done-condition)

decision.choice: Defined RefreshTokenRequest as inline Pydantic model in api/auth.py
decision.rationale: No refresh token request schema existed in schemas/auth.py. Adding it inline avoids modifying a schema file outside this plan's file list, and the model is trivial (single field).
decision.alternatives-considered: Add to schemas/auth.py (rejected: outside T-1-4-4 declared files); use raw Body() (rejected: loses schema documentation)

decision.rationale: Access tokens do not contain a jti claim (only refresh tokens do per plan T-1-4-1). Therefore the current session's jti cannot be extracted from the access token at the route layer. The revoke_session service guard against self-revocation is bypassed at this endpoint but can be enabled if the client passes the session ID via a separate mechanism in a future iteration.
decision.alternatives-considered: Extract jti from access token (rejected: access tokens have no jti per spec); always block self-revocation by comparing path param to user's sessions (rejected: requires extra DB query in handler, violating thin-routes rule)
